  • Post

    Looking ahead to the next 20 years, the Gates Foundation has three major aspirations to guide our work: ​
    ​
    1. No mom, child, or baby dies of a preventable cause. ​
    2. The next generation grows up in a world without deadly infectious diseases. ​
    3. Hundreds of millions of people break free from poverty, putting more countries on a path to prosperity. ​
     ​
    I know that with the right commitment of resources, a fairer and healthier future for everyone is just on the horizon.

    What the Gates Foundation hopes to accomplish over the next 20 years

    Bill Gates on LinkedIn • 5 min read

    5,586 reactions · 1,504 comments5,586 · 1,504 comments

  • Post

    I have always been an optimist. These days, though, my optimism comes with footnotes. For the first time this century, the world slipped backwards on key measures like childhood mortality in 2025, and if we don’t make the right decisions, this trend will continue.  At the same time, I also believe that, within the next decade, the world will not only get back on track but enter a new era of unprecedented progress. As we start 2026, I’m thinking about how the year ahead will position us for decades to come. 

    How to get the world back on track and enter a new era of unprecedented progress

    Breakthrough Energy companies are creating value close to home with projects that create good jobs, strengthen local economies, and help energy innovations reach more people.

    Breakthrough Energy

    5d •

    The best energy companies aren’t just deploying technologies that deliver affordable, reliable, clean energy. They are building in ways that create value where that work happens.

    Across our portfolio, that value looks different from place to place: advanced manufacturing jobs, workforce training, local business growth, school partnerships, community health investments, new markets, and more. We’re proud of how our companies are adding value to local communities.

    We look at how energy innovation can help people capture more of the upside from growth, and why companies that engage and build with communities are better positioned to create stronger projects, stronger markets, and healthier local economies.

    The world needs a plan to ensure that AI’s benefits outweigh the harm it causes, and we need to start now. It’s a monumental challenge that requires us to create new domestic and international organizations, create protections for workers, change our tax code, and much more. Our plan needs to be shaped by people whose voices aren’t often heard in this kind of discussion, including workers, college students, community leaders, religious leaders, parents, and educators. ​
    ​
    If we get it right, the payoff for humanity will be phenomenal and the world will be a more equitable place:     https://lnkd.in/eJGCaqEn

      3d •

      AI will either be the greatest equalizer ever invented, or the worst source of injustice. Even under the best circumstances, the transition to this new AI era will be one of the most turbulent times in human history. How will we use this technology to make the world a fairer place and keep it from widening the divide between rich and poor? How will we protect the people who are most vulnerable to the harms caused by artificial intelligence, including those who lose their livelihoods and the sense that they are in control of their future?

      Answering these questions and acting on the answers should be the world’s top priority. If the world takes the right steps, AI will be a force for good and leave everyone better off.
